data_sources: National Weather Service daily observations, Austin

notes: 42 candidate matches were rejected because the outcome fell on or after the animal's next arrival.

weather_missingness_artefact.note: Full-cohort weather ablation, where the weather columns are missing for every intake after 2020-12-31 and the imputer emits a missingness indicator. On an earlier feature set that also contained two monotone calendar-time features, this configuration showed a spurious +0.0133 AUC gain on the long-stay target: the missingness indicator was acting as a post-2020 era flag. With those time features removed the spurious gain disappears, which is consistent with that diagnosis. The covered-window result above remains the honest test either way.

shuffled_label_control.interpretation: A model trained on shuffled labels should score near 0.5. Anything meaningfully above that would mean a feature encodes the outcome.

monotone_time_features.reason: Monotone in calendar time, so their population stability index against an earlier reference is unbounded by construction and fires in every window regardless of whether anything changed.

calendar_cycle_features.reason: Deterministic functions of the calendar. A single quarter compared against a multi-year reference differs on them by construction, which is the season, not drift.

shelter_level_features.reason: Near constant across animals within a week, so PSI between two windows compares two point masses and saturates around 8 regardless of the size of the real change. Monitored as a level change instead, in shelter_level_drift.

baseline.source: validation block 2019, the last period before deployment

year_over_year_summary.quarter_over_quarter_note: A quarter-over-quarter reference was tried first and rejected. Shelter intake is seasonal, so season and day-of-year change completely between adjacent quarters and the detector returned CRITICAL for every comparison in the series, including the stable 2019 quarters, with season as the worst feature every time.
year_over_year_summary.interpretation: The fixed reference marks every post-shift quarter critical, which is true but never clears. The year over year reference localises the event and settles afterwards, which is what an on-call rota can act on.

lead_time.note: Input drift is computable on the day of intake. The 30 day adoption label does not exist until 30 days later, and a month of labels has to accumulate before a monthly AUC means anything, so performance drift is at best six weeks behind the event that caused it. That gap is the operational argument for monitoring inputs as well as outcomes.

retraining.finding: Retraining did not help. Discrimination was unchanged and calibration got worse. The reason is the calibration block: the second half of 2020 was the most unusual six months in the whole series, and an isotonic map fitted to it transfers badly to 2021. This is the case for a champion versus challenger approval gate rather than automatic promotion, and for choosing a calibration window on stability rather than on recency.

approval_gate.rule: promote if AUC is within 0.005 of the champion and ECE is no more than 0.01 worse

alerting_cost.stable_period: 2019, the validation year, before any known shift
alerting_cost.caveat: The baseline AUC is computed on this same block, so this is an optimistic estimate of the false alarm rate rather than an unbiased one. It is reported as a lower bound.

recommendation.rationale: Keep them only if they buy a statistically resolvable gain and that gain does not shrink across the test period. Otherwise drop them: a feature that a deployed tree model cannot split on is dead weight that also saturates the drift detector.
